info.title: Enterprise Fabric AI API

get.description:
What the sign-in screen may offer (public: no secrets, no user data). In the full
profile it names the identity provider the browser signs in with (M13b/M16).

post.description:
Same reply whether or not the email exists. If it does, the one-time link is
written to the API console (no email server in this project).
Check email and password; on success return a session token.
End this session (the token stops working immediately).

get.description: The signed-in user (used by the UI to restore a session).

post.description: Create a staff account with no engagements, and sign it in. Off by default.
Set a new password with a valid, unused link; sign the user out everywhere.

Re-index one document, one source, or everything (administrators; logged).

A document or a source is rebuilt from scratch even if unchanged, and nothing else is
touched. `all` brings every index in line with the manifest (unchanged files skipped).

Store helpful / not helpful plus an optional correction (masked). Stored only.
Only the person who asked may rate an answer.

Store an implicit signal (copy, citation click, follow-up, rephrase) about one of
the user's own answers. Stored only; the learning loop uses them from M15.

get.description:
The signed-in user's OWN past questions that have an answer, newest first.
Personal to each user: partners do not see other people's history here.

schema.title: Response History Api V1 History Get

get.description:
Reopen one of the user's past answers, in the same shape as the streamed `final`
event. Built only from what was stored at the time: the answer row, its citations
and the agents' trace rows (claim counts from verification, flags from retrieval).

Retrieval and answer-quality metrics, exactly as saved in eval/results/.

Only `retrieval` and `answers` runs count (calibration runs and known-invalid runs are
left out). With `from`/`to`, every such run started in that window is returned, newest
first; without them, the latest run of each type. Never computes or estimates.

post.description: Answer a question, streaming progress, then the verified answer, then citations.

200.description: Server-Sent Events: `progress` (agent steps), `draft_token` (the draft as it is written), `claim_verdict` (one per claim), `token` (the verified answer in pieces), then `final` (a FinalPayload as JSON) or `error` (generic message and a reference).

get.description: The completed answer, its citations and its trace (asker or partner only).

put.description:
Make one routing-policy version the active one.

Allowed when the version has a passing replay report, or was active before (rolling
back to a version that already served users). Everything else is refused.

post.description:
Register a source of documents. A polling source (git, s3, confluence, jira,
sharepoint) is picked up by the connector runner on its next round.

get.description: Document and chunk counts, and last indexed time, per source type.

schema.title: Response Sources Status Api V1 Sources Status Get

get.description: How up to date one source is in the indexes.

Agent-by-agent trace of a query. Partners see everything. Administrators who are not
partners see how each step ran (model, tokens, timing, versions) but not its input or
output: those contain document text and draft answers, and the admin flag grants no
document access.

schema.title: Response Get Traces Api V1 Traces  Query Id  Get

get.description: All users with role, email and engagements. Partners only (emails are personal data).

schema.title: Response Users Api V1 Users Get
